thread:
Ana: Customer on phone reporting spikes from EU customers this morning — consistent reports that requests are landing in us-east instead of eu-west and they see p95 latency ~900ms. They also saw intermittent 502s.
Oliver: Do we have the customer org id? can you paste a recent request id or example span?
Ana: Org: ACME_CORP, example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, sample x-region header from their app: \"x-redwood-region: eu-west-1\" but response headers show \"x-served-region: us-east-1\".
Maya: Hmm, that looks like DNS/geoip mismatch or resolver cache. Any signs of a recent deploy or routing config change?
Cory: No deploys to global routing today. I grabbed a quick dig from one of our EU edge nodes: 
```
$ dig +short edge.redwood.example A
1.2.3.4
;; global TTL: 300
```
But from the customer's ISP resolver we see: 
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 edge.redwood.example +short
5.6.7.8
```
Oliver: 1.2.3.4 is our eu-anycast pool, 5.6.7.8 is us pool. That points to resolver returning the wrong record. Could be EDNS client-subnet/geoip DB mismatch or stale authoritative cache.
Ana: Customer says their resolver is Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and their ISP is using a resolver with stale cache. They also hit a 502 followed by a 429 spike. Could be sticky cache affinity.
SRE-Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-234, assigned to eng-runtime. Priority P2.
Maya: Can you ask customer to run `dig +trace` and paste? Also check CDN/CF cache status for that hostname.
Ana: Sent repro steps to customer. They returned `dig +trace` showing delegation to our NS but answer from their local resolver with TTL 1200.
Cory: TTL 1200 from client resolver -- upstream authoritative probably updated but old cache still held. We also saw our GeoIP DB update yesterday; maybe the client resolver hasn't refreshed.
Oliver: Short term: change fallback policy to prefer regional alias for eu for ACME_CORP and add a header-based routing override (cookie) so their requests route to eu until caches expire. Maya, can you push a route override?
Maya: Pushing a route override to staging now. Patch: added `route_override: org:ACME_CORP -> region:eu-west` with TTL 600.
```
# infra route override
org=ACME_CORP region=eu-west ttl=600
```
Cory: Also purged Cloudflare edge cache and sent purge to authoritative DNS with lower TTL for the next 2 hours.
Ana: Customer confirmed after override they saw requests land in eu-west within ~2 minutes and p95 dropped to 120ms. No more 502s.
Oliver: Follow-ups: 1) Add monitoring alert for cross-region-surge where x-served-region != x-preferred-region for >0.5% of requests over 5m. 2) Investigate GeoIP DB update process and rotate authoritative NS cache TTL policy. 3) Run a probe sweep of major public resolvers to detect stale caches.
Cory: Filed ticket RT-1426 for GeoIP update validation and RT-1427 for resolver probe job.
Maya: Leaving the route_override in place for 1 hour, will rollback after verifying TTL flush.
Ana: Closing loop with customer and asking them to report if they see any regression. :white_check_mark:
CloudOps: FYI — will add probe for 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8/our major ISP resolvers to weekly routing check. :mag_right:
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2026-234 marked resolved (mitigated) at ts=1805550459."
